Slot and pivot capacities and minimum occupancy thresholds for each node type.
Full lock type, ordering and nesting rules for the tree lock outside teardown and recovery.
Memory allocation flag meanings and reclaim guarantees for blocking versus nonblocking requests.
Error pointer encoding and the complete cursor status enumeration.
Gap accounting, tracing and memory ordering guarantees for multi node updates.
Key comparison, pivot selection and boundary arithmetic including maximum key handling.

findings.text: Portable input read interface exposes narrow and wide unsigned reads in native and byte swapped forms plus wide reads with low high and high low device orderings. Each entry dispatches on address range to port or memory access and yields an all ones value when the address is invalid.

Tree teardown and cursor cleanup interface releases reserved nodes and clears preallocation state, drops the root reference, walks and frees owned nodes when present, and preserves only attribute flags while removing height encoding.

Allocation recovery interface reports whether the cursor is in out of memory error state and if so attempts to satisfy pending node reservations, resets the cursor on partial or full progress, and reports failure when no forward progress was made.

Test module entry validates configuration parameters for node counts and search bounds, allocates node and query storage, seeds deterministic randomness, runs basic and search and range and span checks, releases storage, and returns a code that unloads the module, with a separate exit entry that logs departure.

Write preparation entry normalizes cursor state and captures current content, classifies the required store kind by walking to the target leaf, sizes node reservations from tree height and vacancy, and issues nonblocking reservations before any structural change.

Resulting end index for a leaf update starts two beyond the current end then contracts for overwritten span and for alignment of request bounds with slot bounds, so exact edge alignment consumes fewer new positions than interior insertion.

Leaf append preserves trailing metadata when growth stays within pivot capacity, then distinguishes appending at range end from appending at range start from interior insertion, updating affected pivots and published slots and cursor offset accordingly and refreshing gap accounting when either side is empty.

Split and rebalance both proceed bottom up across levels, combining current and sibling extents into a parent update, stopping when a new root is formed or when a single destination remains with no sibling, otherwise advancing height and relocating the cursor to the parent before continuing.

Overflow handling first measures combined data against slot capacity and when overfull probes neighboring nodes left then right for absorption, accepting only fits that leave spare room to dampen add remove oscillation, while underflow handling merges with a neighbor unless the node already spans the full key space.

Store classification prefers root handling for empty or pointer states and spanning handling when the walk crosses node bounds, then recognizes exact fit and whole tree replacement, then selects rebalance for shrunken leaves and split for grown leaves, otherwise choosing in place slot update or node replacement based on read copy update mode and append position.

Node reservation sizing scales with tree height and vacant or sufficient heights, requiring none for in place fits and appends, a small constant for root operations and read copy update replacement, and larger multiples for spanning and split and rebalance paths that may allocate along several levels.

Address dispatch treats high addresses as memory mapped, intermediate addresses as port indexed after masking, and low addresses as invalid with a rate limited warning. Wide port reads pair two narrow reads with order and byte swap variants to match device sequencing and endianness.

Recovery from allocation failure must be called with the tree lock held. When blocking reclamation is allowed and no external lock is in use, the implementation drops the tree lock across the reclaim attempt and reacquires it afterwards, otherwise it attempts reclamation while holding the lock.
Full tree destruction serializes the teardown walk under the tree lock, ensuring root clearing and node freeing and flag normalization appear atomic to concurrent users.

Leaf slot publication follows read copy update discipline with ordered publication of slot contents and pivot updates, and multi node split and rebalance complete with a write barrier replacement so readers observe a consistent generation.

Traversal position is described by a node reference with offset and data end plus covered key interval and depth. Location transfer between cursors copies these positional and range fields together so parent and child views stay aligned during ascent.

Write request state links a cursor with slot and pivot views, request bounds and end pivot, current and new content, computed end positions, and height measures for vacancy and sufficiency, plus reservation fields for pending nodes and staged allocations.

Tree header carries a root pointer with lock protection and flag word where height bits are separable from persistent attributes, so destruction can clear the root and restore only the attribute portion.

Cursor lifecycle distinguishes active and start from paused and none and overflow and underflow and error. Preparation resets nonactive or out of range cursors before capturing content, allocation failure moves the cursor to error, and successful recovery or explicit destroy returns it to a reusable state.

Node reservation lifecycle starts with a computed request count, satisfies a single node from staged storage or a fresh allocation and larger requests from a sheaf with refill, reports out of memory on failure, and can be emptied explicitly to return sheaf and staged memory and clear flags.

Write handling moves from preparation and classification to one of in place update, append, slot store, node store, split, rebalance, or root replacement, with split and rebalance looping upward until convergence and spanning cases taking a dedicated multi node path.

Node allocation can fail under memory pressure and places the cursor in an error state that must be recovered through the retry helper rather than continuing the write, with partial reservations retained for the next attempt and no progress possible if neither sheaf nor staged storage was obtained.

Writes whose affected range crosses slot or node boundaries cannot complete in a single leaf and must take the spanning path, including null overwrites at leaf edges that extend the affected interval into adjacent empty slots.

Invalid low port accesses trigger a bounded warning sequence rather than unbounded logging and produce all ones results, so callers must treat all ones as a possible error indication rather than valid device data.
Port address space offset threshold equals 0x10000.
Port number mask for extracting the low port bits equals 0x0ffff.
Reserved boundary at and above which addresses are treated as memory mapped equals 0x40000.
Invalid read results are all ones per width, namely 0xff and 0xffff and 0xffffffff for narrow reads and 0xffffffffffffffff for wide reads.
